dedupe_keys.name: sewertris synthetic urban sanitary sewer system generator and epa swmm benchmarking framework

description: Kevin Blanco and Gabriel Perez at Oklahoma State University publish SewerTris, a Python system for generating synthetic urban layouts and sanitary sewer networks. Its pipeline creates street and land-use layouts, a synthetic elevation model, a gravity-driven sewer tree, flow inputs and pipe sizes before generating and running EPA-SWMM models through PySWMM. Stochastic ensembles support design and monitoring sensitivity studies. The July 2026 version 1.0.0 archive is free under MIT and describes ten example notebooks using Stillwater, Oklahoma. The tool is intended for configurable urban areas; spatial resolution and simulation periods depend on each scenario. The authors report a test suite and corrected geometric issues, but those tests were not rerun here. Synthetic networks are not observed municipal inventories. The named EPA-SWMM dependency corresponds to model-epa-swmm in the catalogue.
